correctness.rationale: The exact graph model gives forty-two connected forbidden triples; both implementations enumerate 2256 nonempty faces with f-vector (14,91,322,651,728,392,58). A complete 1121-pair acyclic matching is checked on all 10150 Hasse covers, leaving one zero-cell and thirteen five-cells. Forman reduction gives the integral wedge of thirteen S5. The rotation-fixed-face Lefschetz computation yields rational C7 character (13,-1,-1,-1,-1,-1,-1). An independent chain implementation reproduces boundary ranks (13,78,244,407,321,58) over F2, F3 and F5. No unproved attaching maps or inference from finite-field tests is needed.

The earlier Heawood one-independence, matching, two-matching and cut complexes do not imply the two-independence wedge type; their forbidden faces or underlying vertex sets differ. The order-seven rational representation is additional information beyond the nonequivariant homotopy calculation. Specific public-record and primary searches found no equivalent classification; an unindexed computation remains a genuine residual risk.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the smallest cubic graph of girth six and canonically realizes the Fano-plane point-line incidence geometry. Its two-independence complex is the first genuinely higher-independence stage, a natural case outside published tree, cycle and chordal classifications. The exact finite homotopy type (thirteen integral five-spheres, despite nonpure facets) and complete C7 rational homology character answer structurally motivated topology and symmetry questions, rather than an arbitrary graph-count slice. The precisely classified high-symmetry benchmark may inform future higher-independence calculations for incidence geometries.
